posts.author: KiZai
posts.title: Re: Changing from NLR to RJS
posts.html:
Quote from: camper carl on March 04, 2009, 09:43:49 PM
Ok so as i know the server used the new life rule. Which in my experiance enables deathmatching and random money losses. The RJS (relative justice system) works alot better...

Say if person A kills person B, person B can kill person A as long as person A hasnt already been killed. Then once this has happened there is on fued much like NLR just you remember who killed you.

Thats not the RJS, that is just the absense of any rule. There are no benefits to it.

The NLR aims to stop exacly this behavious and when admins are on it is enforced. What you are explaining is a loophole into deathmatching, because after a while you could just kill anyone and say "they killed me first", even though they did it says ago. If the NLR is followed properly, it works:

Quote from: KiZai on February 14, 2009, 10:56:28 AM
New Life Rule (NLR):

When you die, you forget everything that has happened to you in the previous life; you do not know where you died or who killed you so you cannot seek revenge or immediately return to your scene of death. When you are released from jail you also start a new life (unless you are broken out of jail) so the same ruleset must be followed.

-KiZai

As written in the rules thread.

-KiZai

posts.author: Skipper
posts.title: Re: Changing from NLR to RJS
posts.edited: Last Edit: March 05, 2009, 05:39:48 PM by Skipper
posts.html:
Yes, in theory it would work, but can you not see the opportunity for hundreds of random DMs?

It is a lot easier to keep the NLR rather than teach everyone what RJS is. It is very longwinded to explain, as opposed to 'If someone kills you, that's it. Your character doesn't remember. Cos he's dead.'

And typing all in caps is obviously cruise control for cool.

Oh yeah, NLR still allows avenging of your death by someone else who saw it happen, as long as there is a valid roleplay reason.
